weights.csoNote: AAA is LESS common in sub-Saharan African populations than in Western data — basePrior low; but catastrophic if missed. Pulsatile expansile abdominal mass + hypotension + back/flank pain in an older hypertensive smoker.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2014 Aortic Diseases Guidelines (Erbel R et al., Eur Heart J 2014;35:2873-2926); 2024 ACC/AHA Aortic Disease Guideline; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: typhoid ILEAL PERFORATION and perforated peptic ulcer are major causes of generalised peritonitis; board-like rigidity, patient lies still, pain worse on any movement/coughing.
Uganda: sigmoid volvulus, obstructed hernia, adhesions, intestinal TB and malignancy. Constant pain 'out of proportion' + AF suggests MESENTERIC ISCHAEMIA (embolic).

MANDATORY: a pregnancy test in ANY reproductive-age woman with abdominal pain — the core safety rule. Ruptured ectopic = haemorrhagic shock and is a leading cause of maternal death in Uganda. Note: vaginal BLEEDING is captured only loosely via 'vaginal/urethral discharge' (a discriminator gap).
weights.weightCitation: WHO; RCOG Ectopic Pregnancy Guideline (GTG); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Epigastric pain radiating to the back, relieved by sitting forward, with raised lipase/amylase. Uganda: alcohol and gallstones are the main causes.
weights.weightCitation: Revised Atlanta Classification (Banks PA et al., Gut 2013); IAP/APA guidelines; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: common; mimics include mesenteric adenitis, ileocaecal TB, and — in women — ectopic and PID (ALWAYS do a pregnancy test in a reproductive-age woman with RIF pain).

Key MI discriminators 'Exertional' and 'dyspnoea' are NOT in the abdominal-pain capture token set (they exist for chest pain/dyspnoea) — so the EMR currently cannot capture the cardinal MI features in an epigastric-pain presentation. Recommend cross-linking. Rule: ECG in ANY epigastric pain with cardiac risk; DIABETICS may have a silent/atypical MI.
weights.weightCitation: ESC 2023 ACS Guidelines (Byrne RA et al., Eur Heart J 2023;44:3720-3826); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: very common; H. pylori prevalent (not a capture token) and NSAID use. Watch the two complications — BLEEDING (haematemesis/melaena) and PERFORATION (sudden severe pain + rigidity).
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; Maastricht VI/Florence H. pylori Consensus (2022)

weights.csoNote: CHARCOT'S TRIAD (RUQ pain + fever + jaundice) = ASCENDING CHOLANGITIS, a must-not-miss biliary-sepsis emergency; Murphy's sign for cholecystitis. Spectrum: biliary colic (no fever) -> cholecystitis -> cholangitis.
weights.weightCitation: Tokyo Guidelines TG18 (Yokoe M et al., J Hepatobiliary Pancreat Sci 2018); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Uganda: amoebic liver abscess (Entamoeba histolytica) — RUQ pain + swinging fever + TENDER hepatomegaly, strongly male-predominant; right-sided pleuritic/shoulder-tip referral; 'anchovy sauce' aspirate. Distinguish from pyogenic abscess and HCC.
weights.weightCitation: Davidson's 24th ed; Harrison's 21st ed (amoebic liver abscess)

weights.csoNote: Cardinal features — LOIN-TO-GROIN radiation and HAEMATURIA — are not precisely tokenised ('Radiation to back', 'Colicky', 'dysuria' are proxies). The patient is classically RESTLESS/writhing (unlike the lying-still of peritonitis) — a discriminating behavioural sign that isn't captured. CT-KUB is diagnostic where available.

Very common in Uganda (faecal-oral; contaminated water/food, only loosely tokenised as 'high-risk exposure') — basePrior high but study-dependent. The must-not-miss complication is ILEAL PERFORATION in the 2nd-3rd week (sudden worsening + peritonism + distension) — a leading cause of typhoid mortality; the Sudden/Worse-on-movement weights flag that transition.
weights.weightCitation: WHO typhoid/enteric fever guidance; Uganda Clinical Guidelines 2023; Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: Must EXCLUDE ectopic first (pregnancy test) in any reproductive-age woman. Cardinal sign — cervical motion tenderness — is an examination finding, not in the token set. Overlaps appendicitis and ectopic; can cause tubo-ovarian abscess, Fitz-Hugh-Curtis (RUQ) and infertility. Uganda: common given the high STI/HIV burden.
weights.weightCitation: WHO STI Guidelines; CDC STI Treatment Guidelines (2021); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss — pin only in known sickle-cell disease; basePrior population-dependent (high SCD prevalence in Uganda). Abdominal vaso-occlusive crisis MIMICS a surgical abdomen; SCD also predisposes to pigment-stone cholecystitis and splenic/hepatic SEQUESTRATION. Always exclude a precipitating infection and a true surgical cause.
weights.weightCitation: ASH Sickle Cell Disease Guidelines (2020); Davidson's 24th ed

weights.csoNote: CONDITIONAL must-not-miss and a CLASSIC TRAP: DKA causes abdominal pain + vomiting that mimics a surgical abdomen and RESOLVES with DKA treatment — do not rush to laparotomy, but don't miss a true surgical precipitant either. CHECK GLUCOSE + KETONES in any abdominal pain (DEFG). New-onset DKA may lack a diabetes label, so the polyuria/polydipsia feature also triggers the pin.
weights.weightCitation: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS Consensus on Hyperglycaemic Crises (DKA/HHS), Diabetes Care 2024; Davidson's 24th ed
